description: The resolve stage: every output field traces to its base columns through aliases, joins, CTEs, subqueries, set operations and views; a name that doesn't bind denies.

cases.sql: SELECT id, email FROM users

cases.name: aliases and a join
cases.sql: SELECT u.email AS contact, o.total FROM users u JOIN orders o ON o.user_id = u.id

cases.name: JOIN USING merges the join column from both sides
cases.sql: SELECT id FROM y JOIN archive USING (id)

cases.name: an unqualified column present on both sides of a plain join is ambiguous
cases.sql: SELECT id FROM y JOIN archive ON y.n = archive.n

cases.name: a CTE carries its lineage
cases.sql: WITH big AS (SELECT user_id, total * 2 AS doubled FROM orders) SELECT doubled FROM big

cases.name: a subquery in FROM with column aliases
cases.sql: SELECT a FROM (SELECT email FROM users) AS s(a)

cases.name: a UNION's columns take lineage from both arms
cases.sql: SELECT name FROM users UNION ALL SELECT title FROM posts

cases.name: a scalar subquery's value flows to the output
cases.sql: SELECT (SELECT max(total) FROM orders o WHERE o.user_id = u.id) AS biggest FROM users u

cases.name: conditions carry no value
cases.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN ssn = 'x' THEN 'yes' ELSE 'no' END AS flag, EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders) AS any FROM users

cases.name: a bare relation name is its whole row
cases.sql: SELECT y FROM y

cases.name: star expands through the catalog
cases.sql: SELECT * FROM y

cases.name: a view traces to its base columns
cases.sql: SELECT email FROM active_users

cases.name: a view without a definition can't be traced
cases.sql: SELECT id FROM opaque_view

cases.name: information_schema views describe the catalog and need no definition
cases.sql: SELECT table_name FROM information_schema.tables

cases.name: recursive CTE
cases.sql: WITH RECURSIVE r(n) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM r WHERE n < 3) SELECT n FROM r

cases.name: LATERAL sees earlier FROM items
cases.sql: SELECT s.t2 FROM orders o, LATERAL (SELECT o.total * 2 AS t2) s

cases.name: a non-LATERAL subquery doesn't see its siblings
cases.sql: SELECT 1 FROM orders o, (SELECT o.total) s

cases.name: a plain CTE doesn't see itself, so its own name is the real table
cases.sql: WITH y AS (SELECT n FROM y) SELECT n FROM y

cases.name: ORDER BY an output name and GROUP BY a position
cases.sql: SELECT status AS s, count(*) FROM orders GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY s
SELECT nope FROM users
SELECT * FROM missing_table

cases.name: a qualifier naming nothing in FROM
cases.sql: SELECT z.id FROM users u

cases.name: function-call notation on a row (users.f) is not a column
cases.sql: SELECT u.fullname FROM users u
SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = $1
SELECT * FROM users FOR UPDATE

cases.name: XML constructors are not analyzed
cases.sql: SELECT xmlelement(name x, email) FROM users
